# waroom_service_notification_slack_channel (Resource)

Manages the Slack channel that a Waroom service sends incident notifications to.

~> **Note:** A service has at most one notification Slack channel, so manage at most one of this resource per service. Creating this resource overwrites any channel already set on the service, and destroying it removes the channel from the service.

The channel must exist in the Slack workspace connected to Waroom: Waroom looks up its name through the Slack API and rejects an unknown channel ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "waroom_service" "api" {
  name = "api"
}

# Send the incident notifications of the service to a Slack channel.
# The channel must exist in the Slack workspace connected to Waroom.
resource "waroom_service_notification_slack_channel" "api" {
  service_name = waroom_service.api.name
  channel_id   = "C1234567890"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `channel_id` (String) The ID of the Slack channel to send notifications to (e.g. `C1234567890`).
- `service_name` (String) The name of the Waroom service. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Read-Only

- `channel_name` (String) The name of the Slack channel, looked up by Waroom from `channel_id`.
- `id` (String) Resource ID. This is an alias for `service_name`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The notification Slack channel can be imported by specifying the service name
import {
  to = waroom_service_notification_slack_channel.api
  id = "api"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The notification Slack channel can be imported by specifying the service name
terraform import waroom_service_notification_slack_channel.api api
```
